texts: An asymptomatic man with moderate aortic stenosis (peak velocity 3.6 m/s, valve area 1.2 cm², mean gradient 34 mmHg) and a normal ejection fraction needs no intervention now: repeat the echo in 12 to 18 months.
Guidelines advise an echo every one to two years for moderate stenosis, and every 6 to 12 months once it is severe.
Valve replacement is for severe stenosis with symptoms or a falling ejection fraction, or for moderate stenosis when another heart operation is being done.
An exercise test is for apparently asymptomatic severe stenosis, not moderate, and coronary angiography is needed only before a planned valve operation.
In the picture, the bat sleeps under the calendar between the unicorn-and-dragon and the unicorn-and-violin pages, while the stone only half fills the mouth.
Memory hook: half a stone and a happy jogger: let the bat sleep a year or so.
